claims.statement: Selected expert outputs with the same feature width combine by coordinate-wise weighted summation; concatenation would double width for two outputs.
claims.scope: For the specified Transformer FFN expert output width; mathematical weighted sum, not a claim that concatenation can never be used in another architecture.

evidence.supports: y=sum selected p_i(x) E_i(x), collecting expert outputs with a weighted sum.
Sublayers and FFN input/output return to d_model so outer residual is dimension-compatible.
A weights(2,) times outputs(2,2) contracts experts to two features; concatenate yields four.

claims.statement: Direct [0.7,0.4], normalized weights [7/9,2/9], normalized output [7/9,4/9], swapped outputs [2/9,14/9]; swapping both preserves output.
claims.location: 15.5 numerical example, three stated outputs and exercise
claims.scope: Selected probability total is 0.9; feature axis has two coordinates; values quoted at four decimal places.

evidence.supports: Each coordinate and permutation independently calculated.
Float64 computations with independent expected values and correct shapes.

verification.tolerance: Float64 atol=1e-14, rtol=0; actual float32 MoEFFN atol=1e-7; original printed values assessed within 1e-7 of four-decimal decimal targets.

claims.statement: Nonnegative renormalized expert weights give a convex mixture of expert outputs, without ensuring closeness to original input; expert FFN processing and outer residual addition are distinct.

FFN contains expansion, elementwise nonlinearity and return to d_model; residual is x+Sublayer(x) outside FFN.

evidence.supports: Normalized weights sum to 1; arbitrary input proximity does not follow from their output mixture.
Actual expert consists of up projection, elementwise activation and down projection.
Actual model separates expert result h and outer return x+h.
